line_en: I will be straight with you: I believe this is right, and I will say so to anyone.
I am not asking for a favor. I am asking you to look at it honestly with me.
You deserve a plain answer, so here it is: I think it helps, and I will own it if it does not.
I have nothing to hide here. Ask me anything and I will answer.
I came to do what I think is right, and this is what I think is right.
If I am wrong, tell me where, and I will listen.
Think of the families who live with this. That is who I am doing it for.
I have sat in their kitchens. I cannot walk away from what I heard there.
This is about people, not paper, and I think you know it.
When I picture the people waiting on this, I cannot say no.
Someone is hurting right now, and we can end it.
I know it moves you too. I saw it on your face when we began.
People across the country want this, and they will remember who helped.
It is popular for a reason, and it will be remembered as a win.
Stand with the crowd on this one. They are on your side.
Your voters will cheer when they see this come through.
This is the kind of result everyone wants to be a part of.
Be on the side people applaud. It will be a good day for your name.
The numbers back it. Let me walk you through the figures.
Here is the cost, the saving and the timeline, line by line.
The evidence from elsewhere points one way.
I brought the projections. Every one of them holds up.
Look at the data from places that have tried it.
Run the figures yourself. I am confident in what you will find.
Some people want this to fail. Which side are you on?
The opposition will fight us on it. We should not blink.
There are winners and there are those who stand in the way. Choose.
Anyone who blocks this is protecting their own comfort. You are better than that.
This is a fight worth having. I would rather have you in it with me.
Let them complain. We know who this serves, and who it threatens.
Say yes for your own reasons, and let the credit sort itself out.
Let us just say it helps your district, and leave the details out of it.
No one needs to know what we agreed in this room.
Let us call it something that sounds smaller, and it will pass quietly.
You can tell your party whatever you like. I will not contradict you.
Between us, there is room to rearrange this so everyone gets what they need.
I think it is right, and I will say why in plain words.
Fairness is the whole reason. I would not ask you otherwise.
Because someone is better off the moment we act.
Because I have looked the people who need it in the eye.
Because it is what most people want us to do, whatever their party.
Because we can all stand behind this and be proud of it.
Because the evidence shows the benefit outweighs the cost.
Because every measure I have seen points the same way.
Because doing nothing helps only those who profit from delay.
Because the other side has had years and has nothing to show.
Because it is the sensible thing, and sensible people will agree.
Because, put the right way, no one will object.
I would tell them straight what it does and what it costs.
They deserve a plain account, and I will give it in person.
I would introduce them to the people it helps.
Ask the families it touches. They will tell you themselves.
They will see a result to be proud of, and the credit will be shared.
People at home will say you stood with them.
Show them the figures for their own district and let them judge.
I would bring local numbers. They persuade better than speeches.
They will remember who stood in the way, and I will make sure they know.
Those who blocked it will have to explain, not you.
Tell them it is a modest step and leave the rest unsaid.
Say it helps the district and let them fill in the details.
It costs real money, and I will not pretend it does not.
The bill comes due, and I will show you who pays it.
Count the cost of doing nothing, in people rather than yen.
What we spend now, families would pay later.
A fair share from each, and everyone gains. That is a good deal.
It is a price most people will gladly share.
Here is the cost, the saving and the payback, line by line.
The budget figures cover it, and I have the table here.
Those who gain most from waiting can pay the most.
The bill falls on those who can afford it, not on your voters.
Let us not dwell on the figures when the aim is so clear.
It can be found in the budget without anyone noticing.
Things could go wrong. Here is what I would watch, and how I would fix it.
I will own any failure, and I would build in a check.
The greater risk is leaving people to cope on their own.
If it fails, those who needed it most are hurt, and I will answer for that.
We can agree on safeguards that everyone can live with.
A review panel with every side on it would keep us honest.
Regular reports and an independent audit catch problems early.
Trials elsewhere show the failure rate, and it is low.
The risk is from those who want it to fail and will help it along.
Watch the ones who warn loudest. They have the most to lose.
It will be overseen in the proper way by the proper people.
Any problem will be handled quietly before it becomes one.
I would tell your party the truth: you backed what you believe.
If it costs you, I will say publicly that it was my ask.
Your party came into politics to help people like this.
Your colleagues will understand when they hear who it is for.
Your whole party can say it helped deliver this.
Colleagues from every side will be glad you were first.
I can give your whip the figures that show how it helps your seats.
Here is how your own members' districts gain.
Let your party see who is against it. That settles the question.
Those who stay out will be the ones explaining it later.
Tell your party whatever suits. I will not contradict you.
You can credit it to your party's own ideas, and I will agree.
A smaller step would not solve it, and I will explain why.
Waiting has a cost too, and I would rather face it now.
Those waiting cannot wait. A smaller step leaves them behind.
Each delay means someone goes without for longer.
We could start together and widen it later, if you prefer.
I am open to a first stage, as long as we begin.
The trials say half measures cost more in the end.
Set against a smaller option, the figures favor acting in full.
A smaller step is the opposition's way of saying never.
Delay is a decision, and it favors those who oppose this.
Call the first stage a pilot, and the rest can follow quietly.
We can describe it as small now and let it grow later.
You have my word, and I will keep it when it gets hard.
I will not drop it. If I do, hold me to account.
I could not walk away from the people who counted on me.
I made a promise to people, not to a party.
Plenty will stand beside us, and I will not leave you alone.
I will stand with you in public, so you are never the only one.
My record is in the votes and the figures. Check them.
Every claim I make comes with a source you can check.
I will fight for it when the other side is at its loudest.
Others will walk away. I will not, and you will see who stays.
You will have what we agreed, and it need not be said aloud.
Rest easy. I will be there in whichever way suits us both.
I cannot promise it works. I can show what I have and be honest about the rest.
The experts are divided, and I will tell you where.
I have seen it work for people. That is evidence enough for me.
The people who tried it say it changed things.
Places that tried it are glad they did, and others are copying them.
Respected people across the country back it.
Here are the results from places that tried it, with the figures.
Three independent studies agree, and I brought them.
The critics have no evidence at all. Ask them to produce some.
Those who say it fails have never tried it.
The evidence is there for anyone who looks at it the right way.
The experts say what you would expect, put the right way.
I would hear them out, and answer the worst objection first.
They are right about some things, and I will say which.
I would ask them to meet the people they are worried about.
I would ask them to say it to the people it affects.
I would look for what we agree on, and start there.
Most critics want the same ends. We differ only on the route.
I would answer each objection with the figure that matches it.
Their claims do not survive the numbers, and I can show it.
They are protecting their own comfort, and everyone can see it.
Those objections come from people who gain by delay.
I would thank them, agree with everything, and carry on regardless.
Let them think they won the argument. We will have the vote.
Tell me what you need, and I will tell you what I can honestly give.
I will not promise what I cannot deliver. Here is what I can.
I want to help the people you speak for. Show me how.
Whatever helps your people helps this too. Let us find it.
Let us find a result we can both announce with pride.
There is room for a deal that both our sides can cheer.
Put your figures on the table and I will put mine beside them.
Name the price in numbers, and we can bargain from there.
Stand with us and we will not forget it. Stand against us and we will not either.
You will be on the winning side, and it will show later.
Let us agree something and not write it down.
There are things I can arrange that need never be announced.
I would back it even if no one were watching. That is my test.
Because the people it helps have waited long enough for someone to care.
Because people from every corner can see themselves in it.
Because when you weigh who gains against who pays, the balance is clear.
Because the only people against it are the ones it finally holds to account.
Because it lets everyone claim the principle they like best.
I would meet them myself and answer every question they have.
They know someone it would help. Ask them who.
Put it to them as a shared win, and they will take it as one.
I can break the benefit down by town, so they see their own share.
They will notice who fought for them and who hid.
Tell them what they want to hear about it. The details can wait.
It is not cheap. I would rather argue for it honestly than hide the price.
The cost is real, but so are the people who pay for our doing nothing.
Spread fairly, the cost is small enough that few will feel it.
Per household it costs less than a family's phone bill.
Those who dodged their share for so long can carry this one.
The cost can sit inside a larger budget line where no one looks.
I would start small enough to stop if it goes wrong, and say so openly.
I worry too. But doing nothing is the risk people already live with.
Put a cross-party review in from the start and the risk is shared.
I have mapped the failure points, and each one has a check attached.
The only real risk is the people who will try to sabotage it.
If something goes wrong, it can be fixed before it reaches the papers.
I would tell your colleagues myself why I asked you, and take the heat.
Remind your party why they first ran. This is that reason.
Your party gets to share the credit. Nobody stands alone on this.
Your party's own seats come out ahead. I can show you the district list.
Your party can lead on this, or watch the other side take the credit.
Your party can tell the story any way it likes. I will not correct it.
A smaller version would look like progress and fix almost nothing. I would rather be honest.
Half a step still leaves half the people out in the cold.
If a smaller start brings you in, I would take it gladly.
A partial version keeps most of the cost and loses most of the benefit.
Every smaller step I have seen was a polite way to bury it.
Agree to the smaller version, and the rest can be added in committee.
Judge me by what I did the last time it got hard.
I am in this because of people I met. I cannot let them down.
You will not stand alone. I will bring others in beside you.
Look at my votes on hard bills. The record speaks for itself.
Some will fold when the pressure comes. You already know I will not.
Trust that our interests line up. That is better than any promise.
The evidence is good but not perfect, and I will show you the gaps.
I have met people whose lives it changed elsewhere. They are the evidence.
Towns that tried it now hold it up as a model.
The pilot results are in, and they beat the forecast.
Its critics bring opinions. We bring results. That is the difference.
There is a study for every side. Ours happens to be the better-known one.
I would take the strongest objection seriously and change the plan if it holds.
I would ask the critics to spend a day with the people it helps.
I would invite the critics in. Some of their ideas would make it better.
I would answer each criticism with the evidence, point by point.
The loudest critics are defending something they never earned.
Let the critics keep talking. By the time they finish, it will be law.
Tell me plainly what you need. If I can do it, I will.
Help me with this and I will stand by your people when they need it.
Let us make this a win we both can claim at home.
Set out your top priority, and I will cost it alongside this.
Your side or theirs. Choose now, while it still counts for something.
Some of what I can offer is better left off the record.
